sentences.text: Entradasuchus was a crocodyliform, an early relative of modern crocodilians, distinguished by approximately 42 pairs of armor scutes running along its back. These rectangular scutes featured short spiny projections on their rear corners, a unique trait that inspired the specific name spinosus for the type species.

Adrian Hunt and Martin Lockley described the only known specimen of this animal in 1995 after finding it in the Entrada Sandstone at Entrada Ranch in Grand County, Utah. They initially classified it as Crocodyliformes incertae sedis, a category for fossils where the exact evolutionary placement remains uncertain.
Despite its small size, evidence such as fused parietals suggests that the known specimen of Entradasuchus was an adult.
This creature lived between 165.3 and 161.5 million years ago during the very late middle Callovian stage of the Middle Jurassic.
It inhabited an inland dune environment during this period.
